'''David Naccache''' is a cryptographer, currently a professor at the [[École normale supérieure]] and a member of its Computer Laboratory. He was previously a professor at [[Panthéon-Assas University]]. 

==Biography==
He received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1995 from the [[École nationale supérieure des télécommunications]]. Naccache's most notable work is in [[public-key cryptography]], including the [[cryptanalysis]] of [[digital signature]] schemes. Together with [[Jacques Stern (cryptographer)|Jacques Stern]] he designed the similarly named but very distinct [[Naccache-Stern cryptosystem]] and [[Naccache-Stern knapsack cryptosystem]].

In 2004 David Naccache and [[Claire Whelan]], then employed by [[Gemplus International]], used [[image processing]] techniques to uncover [[Redaction|redacted]] information from the declassified 6 August 2001 [[President's Daily Brief]] ''[[Bin Ladin Determined To Strike in US]]''. They also demonstrated how the same process could be applied to other redacted documents.<ref>{{cite news |first=John |last=Markoff |author-link=John Markoff |title=Illuminating Blacked-Out Words |work=The New York Times |date=10 May 2004 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/05/10/technology/10crypto.html |access-date=16 April 2009 |url-status = dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090506200610/http://www.nytimes.com/2004/05/10/technology/10crypto.html |archive-date=May 6, 2009 }}</ref>

Naccache is also a [[visiting professor]] and [[researcher]] at the [[Information Security Group]] of [[Royal Holloway, University of London]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.isg.rhul.ac.uk/bin/staff-dir.php?type=V|title=Information Security Staff Directory|website=Information Security Group|access-date=2019-05-17|archive-date=2022-11-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221130154207/http://www.isg.rhul.ac.uk/bin/staff-dir.php?type=V|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2021, two epidemiologists denounced David Naccache to the management of the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]]. They accused him of having produced a purported fraudulent report in November 2018 for Genevrier Laboratories in exchange for a large payment (more than €250,000) in defence of a delisted drug, [[Condrosulf|Chondrosulf]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=2021-09-29|title=Les expertises suspectes d'un professeur de l'Ecole normale supérieure autour d'un médicament controversé|language=fr|work=Le Monde.fr|url=https://www.lemonde.fr/sciences/article/2021/09/29/medicament-les-expertises-suspectes-d-un-professeur-de-l-ecole-normale-superieure_6096372_1650684.html|access-date=2021-10-01}}</ref>. The lawsuit has been declined by a judgment of the Cour supérieure du Québec on August 28, 2024 that "warns [the plaintiffs] against diffmatory tourism" with "justice costs in favor of the defendants [who are David Naccache, the ex-minister Noëlle Lenoir and the CEO of Laboratoires Genévrier Dominique Vacher]".

== Awards ==
In 2020 Naccache was listed as a Fellow of the IACR, the [[International Association for Cryptologic Research]], "for significant contributions to applied cryptography in industry and academia, and for the service to the IACR."[https://www.iacr.org/fellows/2020/naccache.html]
